finding: Per-season ACL risk: girls soccer 1.08%, basketball 1.03%, gymnastics 1.01%; boys football 0.82%, lacrosse 0.64%, soccer 0.35%; boys basketball 0.25%; 1,389 ACL injuries over 19.1M AEs
status: For full paper; not used in current analysis
caveats: Abstract gives per-season risks without CIs; girls lacrosse not reported in abstract; one club IR in abstract appears to contain a decimal error (verify in full text)

finding: Female:male ACL risk ratio 3.12 in soccer (per AE) and 4.14 in basketball
Club participation RR 3.94 per AE but 1.57 per hour of exposure
caveats: Effect size depends heavily on exposure definition

finding: ACL rate per 100,000 AEs (2007-2022): girls soccer 13.3, basketball 12.2, lacrosse 10.4, volleyball 3.2; boys football 12.6, lacrosse 7.8. Girls' sports +32.3%, boys' +14.5%; girls volleyball +96.7%
source: National ACL Injury Coalition analysis (Aspen Institute Project Play / HSS) 2023
caveats: Coalition report; not peer reviewed; no CIs

finding: Non-contact share of ACL injuries: girls' sports 57.5%, boys' sports 39.7%; girls lacrosse 82.5%
status: Candidate replacement for noncontact_f / noncontact_m in full paper

finding: Girls ACL rate per 100,000 AEs (2009-10): soccer 14.1, basketball 7.7, volleyball 4.5, softball 2.3; boys volleyball 0 in one study
source: Lower Extremity Review summary of RIO and Swenson et al. 2013
caveats: Secondary source; older data; locate primary RIO reports

finding: 21/24 injuries non-contact, 17/24 in games, 20/24 on turf, 20/24 wearing cleats; only 2/24 did a prevention program; game knee-injury risk 0.17 (2023) to 0.64 (2024) per 1000 AEs
population: Girls high school flag football (California CIF)
source: Grewal et al. 2026 J Pediatr Orthop 46(6):e571-e576
caveats: All serious knee injuries (not only ACL); games only; single region; not comparable to ACL rates per AE

finding: Share of injuries that were ACL tears higher on turf: football IPR 1.23 (1.03-1.47), girls soccer IPR 1.53 (1.08-2.16); boys soccer not significant
source: Epidemiological Comparison of ACL Injuries on Different Playing Surfaces in High School Football and Soccer (PMC9083053)
caveats: IPR is a proportion of injuries not a rate per exposure

finding: All injuries 58% more likely on turf (RR 1.59); football, girls and boys soccer elevated
No significant difference in match ACL rates grass vs turf (IRR 0.93, 0.84-1.03); practice on grass higher
source: Howard et al. 2020 Orthop J Sports Med

finding: Braced cadets had fewer knee injuries and MCL tears; fewer ACL tears but underpowered; benefit mainly in defensive players
source: Sitler et al. 1990 Am J Sports Med 18:310-315
caveats: Single dated trial; designed for lateral-blow (MCL) protection

finding: NFL offensive linemen bracers had lower major knee injury rate (0.013 vs 0.049 per player)
source: Ackerman et al. 2023 Orthop J Sports Med

finding: AAOS: prophylactic bracing may have a role in MCL protection for select football positions
caveats: No evidence found for non-contact ACL prevention in girls' sports

finding: Conical vs blade OR 2.02 (0.97-4.20); conical vs turf shoe OR 2.87 (1.58-5.23); cleat vs turf shoe OR 2.57 (1.50-4.40)
population: Female soccer and lacrosse athletes (128 cases / 128 controls)
source: Cass et al. 2025 Orthop J Sports Med
caveats: Recall bias and confounding (turf shoes may be worn at lower levels or in practice)

finding: Elliptical cleats produced greater peak plantar pressure than bladed cleats, contrary to hypothesis
source: Effect of football cleat stud shape sex and fatigue state on plantar loading during lateral cutting (PMC12161356)
